title: StericX: physical-organic molecular featurization and reaction-selectivity inference
description: StericX is an independent, from-scratch Rust reimplementation of the Kraken Sterimol, coordination-aware buried-volume, and pyramidalization ligand descriptors, with reproductions of two published reaction models: a Ni-catalyzed homo-Diels-Alder (Ni-hDA) enantioselectivity relationship and the Newman-Stonebraker %Vbur(min) cross-coupling reactivity classifier. Descriptor kernels are validated against morfeus to numerical precision (Sterimol R^2 >= 0.9999; buried-volume geometry R^2 = 1.000000) and against Kraken's published values on the authors' own DFT geometries across 1,541 ligands (buried-volume family mean R^2 = 0.9925; Sterimol 0.9887; pyramidalization 0.99998; headline vbur_max_delta_qvbur_min 0.9852). As a single dependency-free binary, StericX computes the same buried volume as morfeus about 14x faster per core on the full library. It is a deliberately honest reproduction that leads with its negative results rather than hiding them: StericX's compact native descriptors do NOT model Ni-hDA enantioselectivity (leave-one-out Q^2 ~ 0.002), and a genuine kernel bug surfaced at library scale was fixed and documented in full. It also places a frozen, cryptographically hashed, pre-registered prospective prediction -- with per-ligand uncertainty, an applicability domain, and an explicit falsification protocol -- on the record. Dual-licensed under MIT OR Apache-2.0. Version 0.2.0 turns the descriptors into a selection tool: a precomputed database of all 1,541 Kraken phosphines (StericX's own computed values, aggregated from 31,611 DFT conformers), similarity search in standardized descriptor space, constraint queries over any descriptor, side-by-side ligand comparison scaled to library standard deviations, and reaction-model screening that reports leverage-based applicability-domain warnings and Student-t prediction intervals so an extrapolated prediction is flagged rather than presented as trustworthy.
